Space plays it again

On its own plays a real recording of the single sound, with no word around it — one speaker per sound. In a word plays a short word spoken by your browser, and the word never contains any of the other choices, so only one answer fits. Nonsense syllables such as ba da ga are not used because speech synthesis cannot be trusted to read spellings like thah or zhah.

Word lookup · type a word or a sentence

Words in the built-in dictionary are tagged dictionary. Anything else is spelled out by letter-to-sound rules and tagged guess — English spelling has too many exceptions for rules alone, so treat those as a rough reading. Tap any symbol for its articulation.

Space replays · 1–4 answers

Minimal pairs · one phoneme apart

Cambridge conventions: a dot marks a syllable break (ˈkʌmf.tə.bəl), UK transcriptions print a final r that is only sounded before a vowel (car /kɑːr/), and əl ən are written in full rather than as syllabic consonants. Single sounds are played from real recordings by Wikimedia Commons contributors, used unchanged under CC BY-SA 3.0; each sound panel names its own recording. Example words are spoken by your browser. The articulation drawings are schematic — for real MRI and ultrasound of each sound, see Seeing Speech.
